title: Space Wars
shortDescription: Larry Rosenthal's seminal duel game that introduced commercial vector beam graphics and realistic Newtonian gravitational physics to arcade gaming.
historicalSignificance: The first commercial arcade video game to utilize vector graphics technology, adapting MIT's 1962 Spacewar! with dedicated vector monitor hardware and establishing Cinematronics as an arcade powerhouse.

editorialContent.overview: Frustrated that discrete arcade hardware could not replicate the sharp vector beauty of PDP-1 Spacewar!, MIT graduate Larry Rosenthal built his own custom TTL vector hardware engine, founding Cinematronics to produce Space Wars in 1977.
editorialContent.gameplay: Two players command needle and wedge triangular spaceships dueling around a central gravitational black hole, balancing fuel reserves, torpedo trajectories, Newtonian inertia, and hyper-space jumps.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Pioneered the 'Vectorbeam' display monitor, firing electrons directly to draw razor-sharp line vectors instead of conventional raster pixel scanlines.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Ignited the Golden Age vector gaming craze, directly paving the way for Atari's Asteroids, Lunar Lander, Battlezone, and Tempest.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Vector CRT monitors are exceptionally rare and delicate; preserved in major computer museums and emulated via vector simulators.

awards: Top Earning Video Game of 1978 (RePlay Magazine)

technicalSpecs.resolution: Electrostatic vector beam monitor (infinite line resolution)
